correctness.rationale: Every diameter pair is a vertex pair by strict convexity of squared Euclidean distance in each variable. The strict support-angle inequalities on both tangent cones justify finite local piecewise-linear coordinates. Identity ||Y-X||²=(D-s)²+||w||² is exact; uniform implicit radial expansion and exact Dirichlet boundary moments prove both coefficients with O(epsilon^(2d+2)) remainder. Cone triangulations partition tangent regions and cannot change either integral. The box formula follows from direct coordinate projection, and fixed-volume AM–GM proves unique cube equality. A separate high-precision rectangle difference-density quadrature corroborates the second coefficient; numerical tests are not the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The leading cube-order tail and related sample-diameter limits are antecedents and are expressly excluded from claims of novelty. Their projection-based leading-order asymptotics do not determine the coefficient of epsilon to power 2d+1, which is a quadratic transverse Euclidean correction. Sample-maximum statements for the ball cannot imply all-polytope two-term expansions.

originality.rationale: First-public motivating paper Wang (2026-10-01) treats the same pair-distance distribution but not the diameter-endpoint two-term expansion. The closest full-text antecedent Lao (2010) covers a leading sample-diameter regime for cubes and polygons; the leading cube phenomenon is not called new. Mayer–Molchanov (2006) concerns smooth ball distance extremes, not arbitrary polytopal vertex-cone second coefficients. Detailed claim-versus-implication comparison did not identify a dominating theorem, while leaving genuine priority uncertainty.
residual_risks: Possible equivalent second-order endpoint calculations in older unindexed geometric-probability or stochastic-geometry literature.
Existing leading cube and related polygon extreme-sample results are not original and are not claimed as such.

value.rationale: For every fixed full-dimensional convex polytope the first two nonzero upper-tail coefficients are computable from finite local cone data, not just an order estimate. The universal 2d exponent quantifies how vertex singularities control rare long pairs; the positive next correction measures transverse Euclidean geometry absent from first-order projections. The fixed-volume orthotope bound is sharp with unique cube equality, providing a natural nontrivial shape comparison, without claiming a global inequality for all convex bodies.
